name: pico
short: An LLM-backed Discord presence that decides whether to react, then acts only via tools
description: Pico watches messages in servers where it's enabled, decides whether a message deserves a reaction, and if so, acts exclusively through a bounded tool-calling loop -- never a raw LLM text send. Ships a reply tool, whatever any other cog has registered into corridor's cross-cog tool registry, and one consult_<agent> A2A client tool per agent currently registered in corridor's agent directory (see docs/agent-directory-design.md) -- pico is the sole A2A coordinator; it delegates sub-tasks to whichever agents (architect, or any future one) are currently registered, with no per-agent configuration needed.
end_user_data_statement: This cog reads Discord messages in servers where it is enabled and sends the triggering message and recent channel history (message content with author display names) to corridor's configured LLM endpoint; if the LLM consults another agent (architect, painter, animator or a bootcamp agent), the LLM-written request is sent to that agent over A2A. None of it is stored: the cog stores only per-server enabled state and bot-owner prompt and turn-budget settings.
install_msg: Install corridor too ([p]cog install pixel-agents-cogs corridor); it loads automatically. Outside services: in servers where it is enabled, pico sends message content and recent channel history to corridor's LLM endpoint, and prompts to any A2A agent it consults. Setup: [p]corridor llm endpoint/key/model (bot owner), then [p]pico enabled true in a server (off by default). It reads messages, so the bot needs the message content intent.
author: Pixel Agents HQ Contributors
